text: The rejection is the reject branch of the one published committee-decision operation, POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision (API-S7-002) on /api/recovery/writeoff/v1 with right A, taking a CommitteeDecision and answering a DecisionLogEntry; the element names, the status codes and the right are copied from TSD S7 T-A.1 and T-A.2, each error condition is bound to one message of the legacy set, and no second path is declared.
why: TSD S7 T-A.1 publishes the operation with the request CommitteeDecision, the answer DecisionLogEntry and the right A, and T-A.2 gives the error status codes with no message ID per condition. TSD S7 T3.1 gives no property of either element. Declaring a second operation for the reject, or leaving the element names to the builder, would invent an interface the sources do not have.
read: TSD S7 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T3.1; FSD S7 A2.7.2; legacy RWB-E6-019 Endpoints and Validation and messages; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13 and R5.4 class H
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6019-APP sections 1, 4, 7, 12.1 and 13; RWB-S7-E6019-CON sections 2, 3, 7 AC1, 8 BR12, 12.1 and 19
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-writeoff tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: Both stories build the reject behind the published operation, and a build that adds a second path fails the contract review

text: The reject reason is declared as free-text decision_reason, required on a reject and recorded in the decision record and in the case move, and the decision code the record carries keeps a placeholder value set; neither has a column in write_off, a field ID, a length or a list of values in any source.
why: R-WO-16 and R-WO-18 turn on decision_reason, the FSD field catalog of A2.7.3.2 names no reason or code field, TSD S7 T3.1 lists no reason column and TSD S7 T3.2 publishes no list of values at all. Inventing a column, a field ID, a length or an enumeration would be a business value, and adopting the ledger field name decision_code without its value set would invent the code the reject writes.
read: FSD S7 A2.7.3.1 and A2.7.3.2; TSD S7 T3.1 and T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-16 and R-WO-18; legacy RWB-E6-019 AC1, AC2 and Data
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6019-APP sections 3, 4, 8 BR3, 11 and 13; RWB-S7-E6019-CON sections 7 AC2, 8 BR7, 11 and 12.1
confirm: Business lead and the rwb-writeoff tech lead, before wave 4 starts
impact: The reason is validated as present and stored with the record, the code set is a placeholder, no column and no enumeration is added, and a later reference-data list can be introduced as an additive change

text: The case and the move are consumed from rwb-case: the rejection answers RETURNED_TO_PURSUE on the child-workflow boundary as the stage outcome the parent CaseWorkflow applies, a REST case-move operation carries a placeholder name, and the onward path of a case from RETURNED_TO_PURSUE is published by no row of TSD S7 T4 and stays with the case owner.
why: No source publishes a REST operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, and the connection-matrix row for S7 names Temporal to P7 and P8 with REST and events to P1 only. rwb-case owns recovery_case and every route state, and TSD S7 T4 closes at R-WO-25 plus 'and 26 more', so no published row leaves RETURNED_TO_PURSUE.
read: Context pack connection-matrix row S7; TSD S7 T4 and T3.3; context pack Temporal and Drools slide 13 (parent and children); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and DP-12
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6019-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 8 BR4, 9 and 12.2; RWB-S7-E6019-CON sections 7 AC3, 8 BR3, 9, 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-case owner, before the contract is tagged
impact: The app story answers RETURNED_TO_PURSUE with the reason and the rule version and writes no case row, and the onward path is tracked for the next planning cut

text: The WO rule package is read as data at its version in force and evaluated by this service's own evaluator inside the workflow activity; no embedded Drools kit row is added to the metadata, so RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON are recorded as absent.
why: DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, yet the step evaluates R-WO-16 and the refusal of R-WO-18 of the WO route set of 51 rules over 27 states, and the architecture places rule evaluation inside the owning service's activity. Keeping the plan's H row unchanged and recording the kit as a tracked dependency is the only choice that does not invent a metadata value.

impact: The package arrives on its read with the version recorded with each outcome, and the kit dependency is tracked rather than added to the metadata row

text: This step publishes no event: WriteOffApproved (EV-24) belongs to RWB-S7-E6021-APP, the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as a missing H row, write_off keeps no route state of its own and no column of it is written by a rejection, and the credit-committee rejection of R-WO-14 belongs to RWB-S7-E6018-APP.
why: The service owns topic rwb.writeoff.events.v1 and event EV-24, and a rejection approves nothing, posts nothing and changes no amount, so an event or a write here would be a business value invented by the builder. DP-09 is absent from the pattern set of this key, TSD S7 T3.1 gives write_off no route state and no reason column, and R-WO-14 starts from ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE, a state this step never reaches.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09, DP-14 and R5.7; context pack service rows (topic, event EV-24); TSD S7 T3.1, T4 and T5.3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-14 and R-WO-16

impact: No outbox row, no producer group and no write_off column write at this step, and an absence test fails a build that adds one

text: The role wording of R-WO-16 is resolved toward the permission table and TSD S7 T6.1: the committee decision is exercised by the roles that hold Write-off and posting right A - RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE - and 'Case owner', the owner column of the rule row, is read as the business owner of that decision rather than as a Workbench role of its own.
why: The Business Rules and Routing Logic row R-WO-16 names 'Case owner' as the owner, FSD S7 A2.7.3.3 names 'Write-off committee member' as the primary role, and the legacy permission table gives right A to four roles that TSD S7 T6.1 confirms. Taking 'Case owner' as the role would give the decision to a role the permission matrix does not carry for this capability area.

text: REQ-S7-003 - the committee decision to approve, reject or defer is recorded against each account - is the requirement both stories serve, shared with the approval slice RWB-S7-E6018-APP and the deferral slice RWB-S7-E6020-APP; the FSD Requirements served table is taken over the TSD S7 T8 map, which assigns all eight REQ-S7 rows to FEAT-WOF-01.
why: Template and Rules v1 R7.3 takes the value from the first source that has it, and the FSD publishes one requirement for the three decisions while the TSD traceability table maps every requirement to the first feature. Splitting the requirement into three invented IDs would misattribute the deliverable, and adopting the TSD map would leave the reject untraced.
